<reason>A offered the stronger comparative case: mandatory publication and reviewable explanations can challenge official forecasts without requiring obedience to market prices. A answered both pressure questions directly, conceded genuine manipulation risks, and explained safeguards and permissible discounting. B’s strongest remaining objection concerned manipulation during the decision window, but its case suffered from inaccurate claims about trading rewards and repeated insistence that consultation must mean either compulsion or theater. B’s closing also called oversight and timing objections unanswered despite A’s explicit preceding response.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A exposed that B’s obedience-or-theater dilemma would equally undermine expert consultation. Preannounced quality criteria and public explanations provide a coherent middle ground: officials retain decision authority while their treatment of competing forecasts becomes scrutinizable.</best_rebuttal>
